title: Codex ignores a project's .codex config until the project is trusted
body: Expect the hooks scripts/install-codex.mjs writes (.codex/hooks.json) to be absent until the user trusts the project in an interactive Codex session and trusts the hooks in /hooks; project skills in .agents/skills still load without trust. Do not try to force trust from the agent: a -c projects.'<path>'.trust_level="trusted" override did not make `codex exec` load the project layer. Ask the user to open the project in codex once, accept trust, approve the hooks, then run the live check. Why: on 2026-09-24 (codex-cli 0.154.0) a scratch project with a correct DD config ran codex exec with a working model, loaded the dd-* skills, and reported no DD at all, with and without the -c trust override. Trusted project keys in ~/.codex/config.toml are lowercase Windows paths. On 2026-10-21 (codex-cli 0.163.0) `codex exec` loaded the skills ($dd-recall invokes one) and ran no hook in an untrusted scratch project; its `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust` flag exists but the agent's permission classifier refuses it.
not_derivable: Codex's trust gate is not in its documentation; a correct config loading nothing was found live.

evidence.summary: Codex install, trusting the project and its hooks, moved from docs/integrations/codex.md on 2026-10-21.
Codex install steps include trusting the project and hooks.
2026-10-21: codex exec 0.163.0 in an untrusted scratch project listed dd-save, dd-recall and dd-review, said a user invokes one as $dd-recall, and recorded no hook payload.
